title: Sex-modified exercise ST depression did not improve Cleveland-to-Hungary coronary disease prediction
abstract: In public UCI Heart Disease patient records, adding female-by-standardized-ST-depression and female-by-squared-ST-depression terms to a source-fitted flexible additive model increased Hungarian-site Brier error from 0.141463 to 0.142625 (n=293; difference +0.001162, joint source-refit/target bootstrap 95% interval [-0.003606,+0.009494]). Source cross-validation also worsened. Secondary Swiss results reversed direction when zero-coded cholesterol was treated as missing. This exploratory multi-site analysis does not establish incremental diagnostic value, equivalence, or absence of sex-related exercise physiology.
